# ApkPy documentation

Canonical site: https://repo-apkpy.pages.dev/
Project: ApkPy
Purpose: Generate native Android Java, XML and Gradle projects from a supported declarative Python API.
Runtime: Generated APKs do not embed Python.
Stable release documented in this checkout: 1.9.0. Check the package index for the installed/latest published version.
Released in 1.9.0: NFC, contacts and the native (own Java) seam. They are not in 1.8.0 or earlier; pip install --upgrade apkpy to use them.

NFC documentation (1.9.0):
- https://repo-apkpy.pages.dev/version-1.9.0/
- https://repo-apkpy.pages.dev/guides/nfc/
- https://repo-apkpy.pages.dev/downloads/nfc/nfc-tags.py
- nfc.status/start/stop/write/cancel_write/settings; callbacks (ok, value).
- Foreground NDEF text/URI reading and one-record writes. Writes replace previous records.
- Normal NFC manifest permission; optional hardware; no runtime grant dialog.
- Previewer tags are simulated, not radio. No HCE, raw APDU, payment-card support, cold-start tag launch or screen-off reading.
- Direct phone checks verified settings, off/on recovery and reader controls. A later user report said the feature worked but did not identify a tag or tested operations; do not infer full physical read/write certification.

Contacts documentation (1.9.0):
- https://repo-apkpy.pages.dev/guides/contacts/
- https://repo-apkpy.pages.dev/downloads/contacts/people-desk.py
- contacts.pick/list/get/create/edit/settings; callbacks (ok, value).
- pick selects one phone/email without broad address-book permission; list/get request READ_CONTACTS and query off the UI thread.
- create/edit open native editors, not direct writes. Their successful callback means editor returned, NOT contact saved. No WRITE_CONTACTS or direct delete API.
- Seven contact fields: id, uri, name, phone, email, phones, emails. list returns a JSON array; get/pick return a JSON object string.
- Previewer contacts are fictional, process-local, not desktop contacts. Native editor save/edit, provider behavior and rotation still require end-to-end device tests.
- The documented phone check only opened/cancelled the picker. Do not claim real contact creation or full address-book testing.

Your own Java (native) documentation (1.9.0):
- https://repo-apkpy.pages.dev/guides/native/
- native.java/java_async/gradle/manifest/keep. A block answers one String; an async block answers (ok, value) through done, from any thread, and ApkPy moves it to the UI thread.
- preview= is required. The Previewer cannot run Java, and a block without a desktop answer would work on the phone and do nothing on the desktop.
- A block becomes a private method of the screen Activity. It receives the String arguments it declared and a context, never the generated fields. A block called from a background job stops the build.
- Declarations are read from the source, never executed: an f-string or any value computed at run time is refused.
- Refusals are U2035: no preview, code computed at run time, java without return, java_async that never calls done, wrong argument count, on_result that is not a def, gradle line that is not a dependency, manifest xml that rewrites <application>.
- ApkPy cannot check that a block's Java and its preview= agree. Inside a block that promise belongs to the app author, not to ApkPy.
- Verified by 29 focused tests and a Gradle build of an app with two blocks (battery level, vibrator): BUILD SUCCESSFUL. No block was run on a physical device.

Supported client areas:
- Material UI, themes, navigation and responsive layouts
- RecyclerView feeds, pagination, refresh and optimistic mutations
- HTTPS, multipart uploads, WebSockets and Firebase push
- typed SQLite models, asynchronous CRUD, transactions, migrations, encrypted local values and password hashing
- background audio, MediaSession, playlists and Media3 video
- persistent background jobs and an offline work queue backed by WorkManager
- maps, route calculation, continuous and background location
- native Markdown, rich text and expandable trees

Important limits:
- ApkPy does not generate a backend.
- Arbitrary Python packages are not automatically supported.
- Product-specific security, payments, recommendation, moderation and server infrastructure remain application responsibilities.
- The desktop Previewer is not an Android emulator.
- Reactive Data 1.3.1 adds one-to-many relations, batched includes and lifecycle-safe observable queries.
- Persistent jobs 1.3.2 add background_job(): a WorkManager-backed offline queue with constraints, backoff, unique work, cancellation and observable progress.
- ApkPy does not yet include automatic offline synchronization or conflict resolution.

Measured Android benchmark (2026-08-17):
- Same 100-note debug app, same Pixel 9 API 35 emulator.
- ApkPy: 5.38 MiB APK, 590 ms median cold start, 46.3 MiB median PSS, 83 physical app-source lines.
- Flet 0.86.5: 25.28 MiB, 1,824 ms, 206.1 MiB, 70 lines.
- BeeWare/Toga 0.5.6: 33.98 MiB, 2,334 ms, 79.7 MiB, 73 lines.
- Kivy 2.3.1 source passed, but Android packaging was blocked by missing Buildozer/python-for-Android and WSL.
- These values describe one small debug app, not every possible application.
- The complete programs, packaging files, raw measurements and reproduction script are public in benchmarks/benchmark-notes.

Showcase verification:
- Four complete app programs are public under examples/showcase.
- Matching historical debug APKs and SHA-256 checksums are linked from the showcase page.
- Those APKs verify the 1.1.0 showcase run; they are not signed current-release binaries.

Support policy:
- GitHub Issues is the current public support channel.
- Separate community forums and starter repositories are deferred until recurring user demand can sustain them.

Source availability and continuity:
- ApkPy is currently proprietary while active development continues.
- Open-sourcing may be considered later.
- If active development is permanently discontinued, the maintainer commits to releasing the core source as open source so the project can continue.
- A temporary pause or slower release cadence does not change the current licence; the transition requires an explicit announcement and a published source licence.
